BILIARY SURGERY
Surgical prophylaxis is indicated for open procedures and high-risk laparoscopic procedures. Additional doses should not be given after incisions are closed.

The risk of infectious complications after laparoscopic cholecystectomy is increased after emergent procedures, procedures lasting more than 120 minutes, intraoperative gall bladder rupture or bile spillage, conversion from laparoscopic to open cholecystectomy, and insertion of a prosthetic device.

The risk is increased in patients who have had an episode of colic or a biliary procedure within 30 days before the procedure, patients with acute cholecystitis or jaundice, patients with a nonfunctional gallbladder, patients with immunosuppression, pregnancy, diabetes, age greater than 70 years, or American Society of Anesthesiologists classification of 3 or greater.

If one of these risk factors exists, prophylaxis is indicated for laparoscopic cholecystectomy.  If there is a substantial likelihood that one of these risk factors will develop during a procedure, the surgeon may elect to order prophylaxis.

# If no antimicrobial prophylaxis recommended, select below:

*No antimicrobial prophylaxis recommended

References:

- Bratzler DW, et al.  Clinical practice guidelines for antimicrobial prophylaxis in surgery, Am J Health-Syst Pharm. 2013 vol 70 pages 195-283
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Open procedure or high-risk laparoscopic procedure:

### Preferred prophylaxis

[Cefazolin Weight Based Dosing Preop](surg-cefazolin-weight-based-dosing)

### Alternative in patients with beta lactam allergy

Clindamycin 900mg IV ONCE AND Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV ONCE Preop

## Outpatient

### Open procedure or high-risk laparoscopic procedure:

### Preferred prophylaxis

Cefazolin 2 gm IV over 20 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incision
< OR >
Cefazolin 3 gm IV over 20 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incision for patients => 120kg
< OR >
Cefoxitin 2 gm IV over 20 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incision
Severe B-Lactam Allergy:
Vancomycin 15mg/KG IV over 120 minutes before incision
<AND> Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV over 20 minutes beginning 60 minutes before incision
